tool: ast-grep (winner) vs Semgrep CE, for risky JS/PHP patterns

licences.semgrep: LGPL-2.1-or-later (CLI used unmodified as a dev tool: no copyleft obligation on the team's code; LGPL applies only if they modify/redistribute Semgrep itself)
licences.semgrep_notable_deps: MIT/Apache/BSD only in the venv (click, rich, httpx, peewee, jsonschema, opentelemetry-*, mcp)

install.command: npm i @ast-grep/cli@0.51.0  |  python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install semgrep==1.182.1
install.windows: yes: @ast-grep/cli@0.51.0 optionalDependencies include @ast-grep/cli-win32-x64-msvc, -win32-ia32-msvc, -win32-arm64-msvc (same version); wrapper spawns ast-grep.cmd on win32

semgrep.windows: untested: PyPI DOES ship semgrep-1.182.1-...-none-win_amd64.whl (59 MB; contains semgrep/bin/semgrep-core.exe 255 MB + 17 DLLs; classifier 'Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows'). Not run on Windows here; semgrep.dev docs unreachable (proxy 403) so the official support status could not be confirmed either way. Also needs Python >=3.10 on every dev machine.

fixtures: trials-cloud-2/fixtures/02-patterns/theme (generated by gen.sh; KEY.json): 12 files = 8 seeded (S1 aliased+computed eval, S2 template-literal innerHTML, S3 echo of $_GET value assigned 2 statements earlier, S4 $wpdb->query/get_results with interpolated vars, S5 new Function, S6 document.write, S7 setTimeout string, S8 unescaped href echo) + 4 controls (C1 esc_html/esc_url, C2 textContent + constant innerHTML + 'eval()' in comment, C3 $wpdb->prepare then query, C4 arrow setTimeout + JSON.parse + 'eval(' in comment). S1 and S4 each have 2 locations; a defect counts as found only if all its locations are flagged.

baseline.what: grep -rnE for 7 literal forms (innerHTML\s*=, \beval\(, echo \$_GET, \$wpdb->(query|get_results|get_var|get_row)\(.*\$, new Function\(, document\.write\(, setTimeout\(\s*["'])
baseline.false_positive_detail: C2 (constant innerHTML + 'eval()' in comment), C3 ($wpdb->query($wpdb->prepare(...)) and get_results($sql)), C4 ('eval(' in comment)

candidate_default.config: ast-grep ad-hoc one-liners, no config: eval($X), $EL.innerHTML = $X, new Function($$$), document.write($X), setTimeout($A, $B), echo $_GET[$K], $wpdb->query($S), $wpdb->get_results($S)
candidate_default.false_positive_detail: C2 constant innerHTML, C3 query($wpdb->prepare()) + get_results($sql), C4 arrow setTimeout
candidate_default.note: Same recall as grep; fewer comment hits but plain patterns cannot say 'non-literal RHS' or 'unescaped'. Aliased eval and flow cases are structurally out of reach without rule files.

semgrep_ce.config: runs/02-patterns/semgrep/rules-default.yml: 8 plain patterns (eval(...), $EL.innerHTML = $V, new Function(...), document.write(...), setTimeout($CB, ...), echo $_GET[...];, $wpdb->query(...), $wpdb->get_results(...))
semgrep_ce.false_positive_detail: C2 constant innerHTML, C3 query(prepare) + get_results($sql), C4 arrow setTimeout
semgrep_ce.registry_error: semgrep --config p/javascript -> exit 2: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='semgrep.dev', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /c/p/javascript (Caused by ProxyError('Unable to connect to proxy', OSError('Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden'))). --config auto with --metrics=off -> 'Cannot create auto config when metrics are off'. Registry rules therefore NOT measured.

candidate_tuned.config: runs/02-patterns/astgrep/sgconfig.yml + rules/*.yml (7 rules): js-eval (eval(...) | identifier `eval` not in callee position = alias | window/globalThis/self[non-string](...)), js-innerhtml-nonliteral (innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML where RHS is not a string and not a substitution-free template), js-new-function, js-document-write(ln), js-timer-string (setTimeout/setInterval whose callback is string/template/binary-expression), php-echo-unescaped (echo/print of a variable, property, index or a call whose name is not an esc_*/wp_kses*/i18n/... function), php-wpdb-interpolated-sql ($wpdb->query|get_results|get_var|get_row|get_col whose SQL argument is an encapsed string with a plain $var/$arr[] inside, or a concatenation with a variable; {$wpdb->prefix} is allowed). Why: constraints express 'non-literal RHS' and 'unescaped' which plain patterns cannot; two tree-sitter-php quirks had to be worked around (a pattern with a literal comma needs >=2 args so both arities are listed; a captured argument is the `argument` wrapper node, so constraints use `has`).
candidate_tuned.note: 10 findings = exactly the 10 seeded locations. S3 is caught syntactically (echo of a bare variable), NOT by flow analysis: ast-grep has no taint mode, so `echo $count` of a safe integer would be flagged the same way (WordPress coding standards flag it too).

semgrep_ce.config: runs/02-patterns/semgrep/rules-tuned.yml (8 rules): pattern-either for eval/alias (const|let|var $A = eval, $A = eval), $G[$K](...) with metavariable-regex on $K (constant folding turns 'ev'+'al' into a string so pattern-not $G["..."] hides it); innerHTML with pattern-not "..."; setTimeout/setInterval with metavariable-regex on $CB; php-echo-tainted-request = mode: taint ($_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST/$_COOKIE/$_SERVER[...] source, esc_*/wp_kses*/sanitize_*/intval/absint/rawurlencode sanitizers, echo/print sink); php-echo-unescaped-var (metavariable-regex: bare variable/property/index); php-wpdb-interpolated-sql = mode: taint (any function parameter -> $wpdb->query/get_* without $wpdb->prepare/esc_sql/intval/absint), because metavariable-regex could not see the content of a PHP interpolated string.
semgrep_ce.note: 12 findings on 10 seeded locations: lazy-eval.js:3 reported twice (two eval sub-patterns) and search.php:13 twice (syntactic + taint rule). Taint genuinely tracked $_GET['q'] -> $q -> echo $q across two statements, which ast-grep cannot do. Invalid PHP patterns in this version: '(int) ...' and '"..." . ...' (rule parse errors). CE JSON output hides matched lines/metavars ('requires login'), so results carry only path/line/rule.

limits: ast-grep is purely syntactic: no data flow. 'echo $var' is flagged whether or not $var is safe; '$sql = "... $id"; $wpdb->query($sql)' (variable holding an interpolated string) is NOT caught by either ast-grep rule.

ast-grep PHP quirks (tree-sitter-php): patterns with a literal comma need >=2 args (list both arities); the captured call argument is the `argument` wrapper, so constraints must use `has:`; <?= $x ?> short-echo not covered by the `echo $X` pattern (untested).
The php-echo-unescaped allow-list of escaping/i18n function names is hand-maintained; a new helper (e.g. a theme's own esc wrapper) must be added or it is flagged.

Semgrep registry (p/..., --config auto) is unreachable through this proxy: only local rules measured. Without --disable-version-check a run took 98.8 s (version check against semgrep.dev hangs until timeout).
Semgrep CE 1.182.1: metavariable-regex does not see the text of a PHP interpolated string; JSON output omits matched lines and metavariable values ('requires login').
Semgrep on Windows: wheel exists on PyPI but was not executed here; needs Python >=3.10 on each machine (the team runs Node).
Runtimes measured on a 4-vCPU box shared with other trials; all are sub-second except Semgrep's ~1.8-2 s Python startup.
12 fixture files only; the rule set is 7 rules, not a general security scanner.
reason: ast-grep tuned finds 8/8 seeded defects (10/10 locations) with 0 false positives on the 4 controls and 0 extras, vs grep 5/8 with 3 of 4 controls flagged; it runs in 0.02 s, installs in 4 s / 106 MB as a plain npm devDependency with win32-x64 binaries, and the rules are 7 small YAML files. Semgrep CE tuned also reaches 8/8 / 0 FP and has real taint tracking, but costs 220 s / 369 MB plus Python on every Windows machine, its registry and version check are unreachable here (98.8 s run without --disable-version-check), and its PHP string handling needed a taint workaround, so it is WATCH for the one flow case (request value echoed later) ast-grep can only approximate syntactically.
wrapper: runs/02-patterns/wrapper-sketch.mjs (as checks/patterns.mjs; rules dir runs/02-patterns/astgrep -> checks/patterns-rules). Tested: whole fixture tree exit 1 (10 findings); 4 control files exit 0; missing binary exit 2.
do_not_adopt_notes: ast-grep defaults (ad-hoc one-liners): no gain over grep (5/8, same 3 control files flagged) - the value is entirely in the rule files with constraints.

Semgrep CE as the primary tool: REJECT for this team (Node on Windows): 369 MB Python venv, 220 s install, Python prerequisite, registry/auto config blocked here, 98.8 s run unless --disable-version-check is set, CE JSON hides matched text. Keep as WATCH only for taint-style checks.
Semgrep registry rulesets (p/javascript, p/php, --config auto): not measured, host semgrep.dev refused by the egress proxy (403).

Semgrep patterns '(int) ...' and '"..." . ...' fail to parse for PHP in 1.182.1; metavariable-regex on an interpolated PHP string never matches - the SQL rule had to be rewritten as a taint rule from function parameters, which misses interpolation of non-parameter variables.
